$comment: CE-29 / R4: the browser floor of modern-cmdk's JavaScript, read by tests/unit/browser-floor.test.ts. 'features' lists the web-features ids (node_modules/web-features, pinned in the root package.json) that the built core and react entries (dist/core/index.mjs, dist/react/index.mjs, dist/react/dialog.mjs, dist/react/chunk-*.mjs) rely on without feature detection; every pattern is an AST pattern that must match the built code at least once, so a listed feature that leaves the code fails the test, and every listed feature must be Baseline (low or high). 'floor' is the per-browser maximum of the listed features' status.support, as the test computes it; the docs publish these numbers. 'deny' lists newer APIs, each with its web-features id, that must not appear in the built code: adding a use turns the test red, and 'seed' is the line the test appends to a copy of dist/core/index.mjs to prove that pattern bites. Pattern kinds: call (a call of .method(), optionally on the result of a call to one of receiverCall), member (a property access, optionally on the identifier or globalThis-style property named object), identifier (any identifier of that name), using (a using or await using declaration). Feature-detected uses are not listed (requestIdleCallback in globalThis, the 'Activity' in React check, navigator.scheduling.isInputPending, globalThis.scheduler.yield, navigator.userAgentData). Symbol.dispose and Symbol.asyncDispose are not listed either (explicit-resource-management is not Baseline; ruling R7 makes the core install them with a shim). When web-features is bumped, update webFeaturesVersion after re-reading the data: the test fails until it matches the installed version.
